facts.raw_span: a 4-year history of a left lower eyelid mass
noted by his wife to have recently grown and acquired a crust
a yellowish-brown, well-circumscribed papule was discovered on the central lower eyelid without margin involvement
the tumor had acquired a flakier surface
The specimen measured 0.8 × 0.5 × 0.3 cm
Classic-appearing hyperkeratotic lesion with many pseudohorn cysts
Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells originated from one lateral end, pushing down into the dermis and involving many hairs
Malignant squamous cells contained eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli; mitotic figures were present
Central areas of clear cell change were periodic acid–Schiff positive and diastase sensitive
Negative results with Alcian blue and mucicarmine stains
Negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin and androgen receptor
Ki67 highlighted scattered basal cells and stained about 20% to 40% of tumor cell nuclei

concepts.why: The presence of malignant squamous cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli, as well as the proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells, supports the diagnosis of Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
The classic-appearing hyperkeratotic lesion with many pseudohorn cysts and the central areas of clear cell change are consistent with Keratoacanthoma.

The presence of a yellowish-brown, well-circumscribed papule on the central lower eyelid without margin involvement, as well as the recent growth and acquisition of a crust, supports the diagnosis of Actinic Keratosis.
The proliferation of neoplastic cells and the negative results with Alcian blue and mucicarmine stains support the diagnosis of Sebaceous Carcinoma, although the clinical presentation is not typical.

rationales.F06: Hyperkeratotic lesion with pseudohorn cysts is more typical of keratoacanthoma and actinic keratosis, but also seen in squamous cell carcinoma
rationales.F07: Invasion of neoplastic squamous cells into the dermis is more characteristic of squamous cell carcinoma
rationales.F08: Malignant squamous cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli are typical of squamous cell carcinoma
rationales.F10: Negative Alcian blue and mucicarmine stains rule out sebaceous carcinoma
rationales.F11: Negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin and androgen receptor rule out sebaceous carcinoma
rationales.F12: Ki67 staining highlights proliferation, which is higher in squamous cell carcinoma
